findings.title: Recovery idempotency/latest-pointer writes occur after asynchronous job submission.
evidence: announcement_update.py:1074 submits the worker; lines 1081-1082 then write the deterministic recovery cursor and latest cursor as separate writes.
jobs.py:80-83 persists and queues the job before the API handler finishes cursor publication; jobs.py:103-109 clears the active claim when the job terminates.
announcement_update.py:1041-1059 returns an existing recovery job without repairing the latest pointer; lines 1788-1790 update latest only when it already points to that job.
findings.impact: If the first recovery-cursor write fails after submit and the worker terminates before a retry, a retry can lack the durable idempotency cursor and submit another recovery job. If only the latest-cursor write fails after the recovery cursor succeeds, a retry returns the prior job without repairing latest, so the target-date GET may remain bound to the old job when completion happened before cursor publication.
findings.test_gap: Focused tests cover repeated POST after successful cursor writes, but do not inject a post-submit cursor write failure.
findings.certainty: The conditional code path is supported by source order; whether the storage failure occurs in normal operation is CANNOT_CONFIRM.
